publicReleaseNotes: A failing monitor writes fewer database rows, leaving more room under the daily Workers Free limit. With eight one-minute monitors and one failing all day, a local measurement fell from about 82,300 database rows written per day to 76,500. Uptime groups the failure snapshots from one check and still shows, exports and erases a snapshot for each failed attempt. Snapshots for flow attempts or with screenshots or flow artifacts keep their own rows. No database migrations. Roll back to 0.5.37 or later once a check has failed. After a rollback to 0.5.37, a monitor erasure receipt counts each stored snapshot set as one snapshot. The erasure still removes every snapshot in the set. Product screenshot available from Uptime 0.4.0 at 1440 pixels (.github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png). — Run Edit Run fleet, 2026-11-27
